title: The notebook reviews ask DCLab's leakage decision on their own
request: The owner: continue by priority until tonight's full gate; 22.8 left open that the copilot review and the companion's cell analysis do not ask the decision service on their own.
spec: CAPTURE_AND_DECISION_DATA_PLAN.md 22.8: the technical decision points asked in the notebook companion and the copilot review, the same answer everywhere, a disagreement shown, a person's choice a label.
plan: Read decide.ask and what a name-only state can answer
Tests first for both reviews and the failure path
Wire the companion's review and the copilot's column warnings

decisions.decision: Only the leakage point is asked, from the column's name
decisions.why: a notebook's code shows names, not values; whether a column is an identifier needs its uniqueness, so a name-only answer there would always be no

decisions.decision: A column only the decision flags gets its own finding kind in the companion
decisions.why: the frozen development suite scores prediction_time_availability; a new kind keeps that suite unchanged while still showing the decision

decisions.decision: The copilot shows the decision only beside its own column warnings
decisions.why: the copilot records every column a notebook touches, the target too; new findings there would flag the target as a leak

decisions.decision: The review stands when the decision service fails, and says so
decisions.why: the review is useful without it; a silent gap would read as a clean answer

change: dclab_rnd/notebook_assist.py (leakage_decision, review_document asks it), dclab_rnd/copilot/analyzer.py (Finding.decision on column warnings), tests/test_notebook_assist.py, the 22.8 status in CAPTURE_AND_DECISION_DATA_PLAN.md.

findings.defect: The name rule flags contract_duration as a possible leak
findings.scenario: The churn demo notebook selects contract_duration as a feature.
findings.cause: The name rule's leak words include duration, so contract_duration is flagged although a contract's length is usually known in time.
findings.fix: Kept visible as its own finding, as 22.8 asks a disagreement to be shown; the test now expects it and the plan names it as likely a false alarm a person answers.

findings.defect: The review's limitation line suggested a routed model could answer a name-only question
findings.scenario: The leakage point is routed to a classifier that may act, and a notebook is reviewed.
findings.cause: The limitation line said the rule answers unless a model is routed, but a name-only state has no bands, so no classifier ever reads it and the rule always answers.
findings.fix: The line now says the name rule answers because a routed model needs bands a notebook's code does not show.

outcome: Both notebook reviews now show DCLab's leakage decision on the columns they read, the same answer as the decision API, with its limits written in the review.
lessons: A decision asked from less information than it was built for should say so in its answer, not only in its docs.
Before adding findings to a review, check which columns it reads: a review that sees the target cannot flag every leak-sounding name.
risks: Leak words such as post, after and duration flag harmless names (days_after_signup, post_code, contract_duration): expect noise until a person's answers train a better answerer.
